name: Stripe Create Payment Intent
description: Creates a PaymentIntent object to track the lifecycle of a payment from creation to confirmation to capture. Required parameters include amount (in smallest currency unit e.g. paise), currency (ISO 4217 code), and payment_method_types. Returns a client_secret used on the frontend to complete payment. Supports automatic payment methods, 3D Secure authentication, and metadata fields. Use confirm=true to attempt immediate confirmation server-side.
plain_explanation: This starts a payment request — like opening a tab at a shop. When a customer wants to pay, our backend creates a Payment Intent which tracks the whole payment process. The customer then completes the payment on their side (entering card details), and Stripe handles the verification and money transfer. It's the main way we initiate any card payment.

name: Stripe Confirm Payment Intent
description: Confirms a PaymentIntent, attempting to collect payment from the customer. Can include a payment_method ID or a payment_method_data object with card details. If 3D Secure authentication is required, the response will include a next_action field with a redirect URL. Returns the updated PaymentIntent object with status field: succeeded, requires_action, requires_payment_method, or canceled.
plain_explanation: This is the step where we actually charge the customer. After they've entered their card details, we confirm the Payment Intent to collect the money. If the customer's bank needs extra verification (like an OTP), Stripe pauses and waits for that before completing the charge.

name: Stripe Create Refund
description: Issues a refund for a previously captured charge or payment intent. Accepts charge or payment_intent parameter to identify the original payment. The amount field is optional — if omitted, the full amount is refunded. Partial refunds are supported. Refunds typically appear on a customer's bank statement within 5-10 business days. Refunds can only be issued up to 1 year after the original charge.
plain_explanation: This sends money back to a customer when they request a refund. We specify which payment to refund and optionally how much (full or partial). The money goes back to their original payment method. Note: refunds can take 5-10 business days to appear in their account even after we process it.

name: Stripe Retrieve Customer
description: Retrieves a Customer object by its ID, returning stored details including email, name, default payment method, address, metadata, and the customer's balance. Customer objects are used to store payment information securely and associate charges, subscriptions, and payment methods to a single entity across transactions. Useful for checking a customer's current payment methods before initiating a new charge.
plain_explanation: This fetches all stored details about a customer in our Stripe account — their email, name, saved card details, and payment history. We use it when we want to charge a returning customer without them having to re-enter their card, or to check their account status before processing an order.

name: Stripe List Charges
description: Returns a list of charges for the account, supporting filters including customer ID, created date range, and payment intent ID. Paginated using a cursor-based system with limit (max 100) and starting_after parameters. Each charge object includes amount, currency, status (succeeded/pending/failed), payment method details, and description. Used for transaction reporting and reconciliation.
plain_explanation: This lists all the payments that have been made through our Stripe account. We use it for building transaction reports, checking whether a specific payment went through, or reconciling what customers paid against what was delivered.

name: Stripe Create Webhook Endpoint
description: Registers a URL to receive real-time event notifications from Stripe. Requires a url and an array of enabled_events (e.g. payment_intent.succeeded, payment_intent.payment_failed, charge.refunded, customer.subscription.updated). Returns a webhook_secret used to verify the authenticity of incoming webhook payloads via HMAC-SHA256 signature. Maximum 16 webhook endpoints per account.
plain_explanation: This sets up our system to be automatically notified by Stripe whenever something important happens — like a payment succeeding, failing, or a refund being processed. Instead of constantly checking Stripe, Stripe calls our server the moment an event occurs. Think of it as Stripe sending us an instant alert for every payment event.

name: SendGrid Send Email
description: Sends a transactional or marketing email. Request body includes personalizations array (to, cc, bcc, subject per recipient), from address, content array (text/plain and text/html), and optional fields including reply_to, attachments, template_id, dynamic_template_data, and send_at for scheduled sending. Supports up to 1000 recipients per API call. Requires a verified sender identity. Rate limit: 600 requests/minute on Pro plans.
plain_explanation: This sends an email from our system to a customer — anything from an order confirmation to a password reset to a marketing newsletter. We can send to one person or thousands at once. The email can include HTML formatting, attachments, and personalised content like the customer's name or order details.

name: SendGrid Get Email Activity
description: Retrieves email activity for messages sent within the last 30 days. Supports filtering by to_email, from_email, subject, status (processed, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, spam_report, unsubscribed), and message_id. Returns event-level data showing the journey of each email. Requires the Email Activity feature to be enabled on the account. Results limited to 1000 per query; use pagination for larger exports.
plain_explanation: This lets us check what happened to emails we sent — whether they were delivered, opened, clicked, bounced, or marked as spam. Useful when a customer says they didn't receive an email and we need to investigate, or when we want to measure how many people are opening our emails.

name: SendGrid Create Email Template
description: Creates a transactional email template using SendGrid's Dynamic Templates system. Templates support Handlebars syntax for variable substitution (e.g. {{customer_name}}, {{order_id}}). After creating a template, individual versions with HTML content and subject lines are added via POST /v3/templates/{template_id}/versions. Retrieve the template_id to reference it in the send endpoint using the template_id field.
plain_explanation: This creates a reusable email design we can send to many customers with personalised details filled in automatically. For example, we design an 'Order Shipped' email once with placeholders like {{name}} and {{tracking_number}}, and each time we send it, those placeholders get replaced with the real customer's information.

name: Twilio Send SMS
description: Sends an SMS or MMS message via the Twilio REST API. Required parameters include To (recipient phone number in E.164 format), From (a Twilio phone number or Messaging Service SID), and Body (message text up to 1600 characters for SMS). Optionally attach media URLs for MMS. Returns a Message object with SID, status (queued/sending/sent/failed), and error codes if applicable. Rate limits depend on the destination country and phone number type.
plain_explanation: This sends an SMS text message to a customer's mobile number. We use it for things like one-time passwords (OTPs), delivery alerts, or appointment reminders via text. The API handles the actual delivery through mobile networks and tells us whether the message was sent successfully.

name: Twilio Lookup Phone Number
description: Validates and returns information about a phone number including its country code, national format, carrier name, line type (mobile, landline, VoIP), and SIM swap detection data. Useful for validating user-entered phone numbers before sending SMS or making calls. Add-on packages available for caller name lookup and fraud scoring. Accepts numbers in E.164 format or local format with country code specified.
plain_explanation: This checks whether a phone number is real and what type it is (mobile, landline, or internet-based). We use it to validate phone numbers customers enter during sign-up — for example, to make sure they've provided a mobile number before we try to send them an OTP, and to filter out fake or invalid numbers.

name: Google Maps Geocoding API
description: Converts a human-readable address into geographic coordinates (latitude and longitude) or vice versa (reverse geocoding). Accepts address string or latlng parameter. Returns structured address components, formatted address, geometry (location coordinates and viewport bounds), and place_id. Supports region biasing and component filtering. Billed per request; first 40,000 requests per month free, then $5 per 1000 requests.
plain_explanation: This converts a street address (like '123 MG Road, Bengaluru') into GPS coordinates (latitude and longitude) that can be plotted on a map, or works in reverse to turn coordinates into a readable address. We use it for features like showing customer addresses on a map, calculating delivery zones, or validating that an address entered by a user actually exists.

name: Google Maps Distance Matrix API
description: Calculates travel distance and time between multiple origins and destinations simultaneously. Accepts arrays of addresses or lat/lng coordinates for both origins and destinations. Supports travel mode (driving, walking, bicycling, transit), departure_time for traffic-aware estimates, and avoid parameters (tolls, highways, ferries). Returns a matrix of distance values in metres and duration in seconds for each origin-destination pair.
plain_explanation: This calculates how far and how long it takes to travel between locations — useful for estimating delivery times, finding the nearest store, or showing customers how long their delivery will take. We can check multiple locations at once, making it efficient for sorting delivery routes or showing estimated arrival times.
